title: Implement Commons audio ingestion and production import
description:
Implement the Commons category importer and production-library integration described by the sibling behavior story.

- Enumerate direct members for four configured category pages through MediaWiki API; deduplicate by page identity and preserve every category membership.
- Fetch revisioned file-page content and extmetadata in small batches; normalize only supported license forms with required attribution, and report non-audio or incomplete/unsupported candidates.
- Download eligible audio serially with a descriptive User-Agent, request delay, Retry-After-aware backoff, checksum verification, and resumable/idempotent state.
- Preserve raw metadata/license statements and page revision in Recording sourceMetadata; keep original media source URL and checksum in the source catalog/sample.
- Add Ogg/Vorbis and Opus decoding; analyze/import eligible samples and records into the production library.
- Write Gherkin-backed tests for discovery, pagination, rights qualification, throttling/resume, formats, provenance, and idempotency.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implementation started after fast-forwarding develop. Scope is the four direct Commons categories; eligible audio-only files must have complete supported rights metadata. Work includes API discovery, rate-limited resumable downloads, raw provenance snapshots, Ogg/Opus decode support, analysis, and production-library import.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Runtime Commons discovery found 403 unique direct files across 406 category memberships. 388 audio files with supported licenses and required credits were downloaded serially (5,779,929,792 bytes); 15 candidates were excluded with page-specific reasons and zero downloads failed. The importer now stores full extmetadata and revision snapshots; SHA-256 and source-catalog audit passed. Analysis is running on all 388 files, with native Ogg/Vorbis/Opus decode tests and migration provenance checks green.
